payload.summary: Ward Flow's synthetic patient records are in 1629 published commits under a 2026-08-31 ruling the owner has deferred, not withdrawn
payload.detail: REFRAMED 2026-09-20 after Codex correctly flagged the original wording on PR #2930, and RE-MEASURED the same day after a second Codex review found the exposure figures understated three times running. The original row was titled around the repository contradicting the 2026-09-01 assume-private ruling. THAT CONTRADICTION IS RESOLVED and must not be re-raised: PR #2927 superseded that ruling in docs/ward-flow-owner-rulings-2026-09-01.md with the owner's 2026-09-20 decision, quoted verbatim - 'i will leave it public for now' - and recorded the first actual measurement (GitHub API: private=false, visibility=public). Leaving the row as written would have taught later sessions to treat a deliberate owner decision as an urgent unresolved defect, which is the same absence-read-as-signal failure this ledger exists to prevent. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is the 2026-08-31 ruling, section 5: 'Ward Flow is NOT to be pushed to a public repository as it stands.' The owner has DEFERRED that decision (2026-08-31 community audit, item 9: 'Defer for now - his decision, made knowing the eight invented patient records and three commits of history are public'), and deferred is not withdrawn. THE MEASURED BASIS IS FAR LARGER THAN THE RULING RECORDED. Files, pinned at commit 8d5cea0d1: the UMRNs are in 16 files where the ruling recorded 2, of which 14 CARRY the data and 2 only discuss it, and the names in 8 where it recorded 5. Commits: 1629 published commits carry the records, 1335 of them on origin/main - not the 3 the ruling recorded and every later restatement repeated. THE COMMIT FIGURE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, because it is what the ruling's own argument rests on: 'publishing a repository publishes its history'. Every earlier count used git log -S, the pickaxe, which finds commits where a string's PRESENCE CHANGES, not commits whose TREE CONTAINS it. There are only two distinct versions of src/components/ward-management/ward-patients-seed.ts in the entire repository and BOTH hold the eight records, so every commit carrying that file exposes them. Verified by enumerating the blob at that path across every commit reachable from the origin refs. WHY THE FILE FIGURE IS PINNED TO A SHA: every document that discusses this exposure - the two ruling files, this row, the inbox requests behind it - must name UM10000 or Talia Halloway to discuss it at all, and so joins the count. At the head of the commit that introduced the corrected paragraph the same commands already returned 20 and 12. Quote the pinned figure, never a fresh HEAD count, or each retelling makes the exposure look worse while nothing has changed. THREE SUCCESSIVE MEASUREMENTS RAN LOW, ALL IN THE SAME DIRECTION: 12 files / 4 commits, then 16 files / 3 commits, then this. The 12 came from searching UM100001, the first record of eight, missing four files carrying only one of the other seven. A privacy count is easy to take against one specimen, one branch, or one kind of change, and every such shortcut truncates - toward making publication look safer. Measure containment, not change, and pin the SHA. The records themselves are genuinely synthetic - the file header reasons the choice at length and the screens carry a visible synthetic-data marker - and the ruling's point was never that they are real, but that they do not look invented: eight full names, each with a UMRN and a date of birth, in a psychiatrist's public repository. The two options the owner approved at the time remain the options, and the containment count is the argument for the second: make the repository private, or replace every name and UMRN wherever they appear and publish a FRESH repository with a single initial commit, since rewriting 1629 commits of history is not a realistic alternative. NEXT ACTION IS THE OWNER'S, not an assistant's: this row exists to keep the deferral visible, not to reopen a settled decision.
